title: Streamlined onboarding manifests for eval runner interchange
creator: Arianna Kim
description: Goal: Reduce friction and variability when onboarding new models by standardizing a lightweight manifest and a set of pluggable eval-runner shims so benchmark harnesses can produce deterministic, version-pinned performance profiles across different dataset/prompt variants.
background: Current state: model onboarding requires engineers to wire multiple bespoke dataset formats, prompt variant tables, and runner glue code per model. This leads to non-deterministic sampling, duplicated seeding logic, and brittle profile artifacts that complicate pinning and rollouts. Several recent onboarding tickets required ad-hoc fixes to runner contracts and manual seed bookkeeping (see ENG-21245, ENG-33421, ENG-512304).
proposed_solution: Introduce a minimal onboarding manifest spec and a set of small runner shims that implement a deterministic sampling contract. The manifest will declare dataset fingerprint, accepted prompt namespaces and variant weights, recommended seeding strategy, and required runner capabilities (e.g., streaming, function-calling). Runner shims will expose a stable adapter API used by the harness: init(manifest), sample(batch_id), run(sample), record(metadata). The harness will use these to generate profile artifacts with reproducible metadata suitable for version pinning and automated publishing to the profile registry.
acceptance_criteria: A manifest schema (v1) is published in the model-onboarding repo and validated by unit tests
At least two runner shims implemented: one for the current harness and one for the lightweight executor used in CI
End-to-end pipeline: given a manifest + model stub, the harness produces identical profile artifacts across two separate runs with the same seed and environment
Profile artifacts include: manifest fingerprint, prompt variant map, sampling seed, runner version, model version pin, and per-bucket latency/cost histograms
CI check that validates manifest schema and runs the shim-based harness on a small canonical dataset
Documentation and example manifests for a transformer LM and a chat-model onboarding guide
tasks: Design manifest v1 schema and examples
Implement manifest parser and validator library
Add deterministic seeding utilities to harness core
Implement two runner shims (harness-native and ci-executor)
Wire profile artifact metadata emission and upload to registry
Create CI job that validates manifests and runs a smoke-profile generation
Write onboarding guide and example manifests in docs/confluence
stakeholders: Platform - model catalog and profile registry owners
Developer Experience - docs and example manifests
risks: Overly rigid manifest fields may not accommodate specialized evals (e.g., multi-turn retrieval setups)
Determinism across hardware variants could still differ due to non-deterministic kernels or runtime timing
Adoption friction if manifest authoring is perceived as heavy for early-stage models
mitigations: Keep manifest v1 deliberately small and extensible via optional fields
Document hardware determinism caveats and include hardware fingerprint in profile artifact
Provide generator tools and example manifests to lower authoring burden
notes: This ticket focuses on the harness-side contracts. Follow-up work will be required to integrate rollout automation and canary evaluation using these artifacts. Coordinate with ENG-92784 for profile publishing expectations.
